ranked.verdict: Do not build the Messages page. Build the delivery layer under the request thread, then stop lying on the surfaces a client already sees. Three of the five readers converged independently on the same root cause and I confirmed it in the code: this platform sends zero email for any message, any status change, or any client-submitted request. There are exactly 9 real sendEmail call sites in app/ and lib/ and every one is a document send (invoice, invite, welcome, kickoff, announcement, contract, proposal, schedule). Four finished templates (emails/new-request.tsx, request-delivered.tsx, invoice-overdue.tsx, review-request.tsx) have zero importers. ManyRequests request #203 has 72 comments and #297 has 23 across a month, between people who were mostly not logged in; email is the only reason those threads function. Every other gap here is a rounding error next to that one. Second theme: the client-facing surfaces are honest about almost everything except what a client looks at daily. The home's "ready for your review" counter includes delivered requests forever, so approving makes it go UP. A client submitting a request notifies nobody at Tahi, while a request emailed in DOES ring the bell. Moving a Tahi-internal request pushes its title into the client's bell. Ranks 1-3 plus 5 total 2.25 days and remove every live client-facing lie; rank 4 is 2.5 days and is the actual ManyRequests parity item. That 4.75-day block is the whole cutover-critical answer to the question. On the two sequencing questions asked directly: notifications genuinely do come before messaging (the thread is built and works, it just has no delivery), and time genuinely does come before invoices (the /time form silently discards the hourly rate you type, so anything billed from timesheet hours uses a fallback rate). Contracts, proposals and schedules cannot block a ManyRequests cutover by definition, because ManyRequests has none of them.

ranked.item: Stop internal request titles leaking into client notification bells

Move a Tahi-internal request that carries an orgId and every linked contact at that client gets a bell row containing the internal title, deep-linked to /requests/{id} which app/api/portal/requests/[id]/route.ts:56 then 404s. Both the single PATCH and the bulk PATCH share this helper, so a backlog sweep fans it out at scale. A live violation of the Tier 1 bar in TASKS.md ('a client can NEVER reach Tahi-internal data'), missed by the 423-route audit because it is a notification path rather than a data route. Fix is one field on the interface plus one gate, with a test alongside the existing CLIENT_SILENT_STATUSES coverage.

ranked.item: Notification email dispatcher, wired to exactly three events
ranked.why: The actual ManyRequests parity item and the answer to the question. Verified: 9 real sendEmail call sites in app/ and lib/, all document sends; the four templates above each returned 0 importers repo-wide. lib/notifications.ts has no Resend path at all, and notifyOrgContacts (:360-377) silently drops every contact without a clerkUserId, so a client who has been invited but not signed in gets literally nothing when the studio replies. reads.recommendation:
Do not build the proofing viewer, file annotation, per-request ratings or NPS automation. The live ManyRequests portal proves Liam has never used the equivalents there (rating null, Reviews report empty, Avg Rating 0 of 5), and neither platform has annotation. Building them would be exactly the "nice to haves" he said to stop adding.

The minimum feedback loop for a cutover is four things, roughly 4 days:

1. Make the approval mean something (0.25d). Drop 'delivered' out of REVIEW_SET in client-home.tsx:223 so approving actually clears the prompt, and re-label the Vitals tile. This is a one-line fix on the client's most-seen surface and should ship on its own today. Add the regression test.

2. Email the two events that carry the loop (2d). A client who is not logged in currently learns nothing, ever. Send on exactly two triggers: a request entering client_review ("Your work is ready to review", deep-linked to the request), and a new external message on a request. Reuse the announcement fan-out's contact resolution and preference handling; wire the orphaned emails/request-delivered.tsx rather than writing a new template. Also fix the client-facing notification copy while you are in there - "status changed to client review" is not a call to action. This is the single highest-value day of work in the area and it is what actually replaces ManyRequests, whose entire loop is email.

3. Delete the lies (1d). Remove the /reviews Send button (or make it POST a real outreach email using the existing template and the respond endpoint that already works); fix copyReviewLink to /review/<token>; delete or wire POST /api/admin/health, GET/POST /api/portal/review-outreach and POST /api/admin/reviews/outreach; either submit videoUrl and caseStudyInterest from the review form and accept them in /api/public/review, or cut those two steps and the Video/Clutch KPIs they feed; correct the two lying test docblocks and the ChecklistsPanel comment. Every one of these is a thing Liam or a client will click and be quietly betrayed by, and STATUS.md already treats that class of bug as a cutover blocker elsewhere (deal nudges).

4. Prove it once, as a client (0.75d). Close V1-QA.1: a real client-visible request in client_review, in an impersonated org, on production, at 375px and in dark mode - approve one, request changes on another, confirm the home counter moves and the studio gets both the bell and the email. Then add the e2e that does not exist: the review verdict has one unit test for its fan-out and zero end-to-end coverage.

Deliberately deferred and worth writing down so nobody hunts for it: request steps (schema and API exist, no UI writes them, the client-facing progress bar silently falls back to the status map - either build the admin ticker or stop pretending the bar is granular); client-visible checklists (the portal projection omits the column on purpose, which is defensible, so fix the comment rather than the code); the revision counter (either increment it on a change request or delete the chip - a permanently-zero "Rev 0/3" is worse than nothing); a persisted per-request activity log, which is the one real ManyRequests capability we lack structurally, but it is a table plus a write on every mutation and it is not what a client needs on day one.

The testimonial and case-study pipeline is a further ~3 days to be honest end to end (send the email, persist the video and case-study answers, add the approved-case-studies view Decision #018 promises, read the AI draft back instead of regenerating). Keep it out of the cutover. Liam's own ManyRequests data says he will not use it until the delivery loop is boring.

Unit-test the pref gate and the recipient resolution; that is the coverage hole the audit flagged.

(a) POST /api/portal/requests/[id]/reads (mirror the admin route, userType 'contact') and have the client request detail call it, so read state exists for both sides.
(b) When a request detail page loads, PATCH the bell rows whose entityId matches to read - a bell that never clears is a bell people stop looking at.

BLOCK 1 - cutover-adjacent correctness, ~6d, do first. (a) Fix the time-to-invoice path: persist hourlyRate in /api/admin/time POST, retire the duplicate /api/admin/time-entries or make it the single writer, add a Rate column to the /time table so the value is visible, then give xero-export an idempotency guard keyed on org+month, a billingModel filter so retainer clients are excluded, a UI trigger with a dry-run preview, and a loud 'skipped, no rate' result instead of `continue`. Until this lands, hourly billing is a silent-data-loss path and Liam should not log time expecting to bill from it. (b) Fix the portal project card to require a published snapshot (app/api/portal/project/route.ts:97-101) - one line, and it is the only live client leak in my area. (c) Point the search palette at contract_documents and drop the orphaned contracts table.

BLOCK 2 - the money paths Liam called nice-to-haves but that decide whether a deal closes, ~7d. Publish-before-share on both proposals and schedules (snapshot on share, reject email on unpublished, clear on revoke). Make patchProposal call mutate() so Publish resurfaces after a top-level edit. Close the accept and sign loop: a notifications row plus a Resend email to Liam plus a deal activity on proposal accept, decline and question, and on EVERY contract signature not just the last. Persist the signed PDF to R2 signedStorageKey with a download button. Then the shared deliverable-kit pass: consume --page-chrome-text, add app/p/layout.tsx pinning light tokens, gantt narrow-mode card stack, VariantTabStrip overflow at 375px, real public titles with OG. These are Tier 3 in TASKS.md but they are the difference between "we have proposals" and "a client can accept one on a phone and someone finds out".

BLOCK 3 - /reports triage, ~4d, and it is mostly deletion. The page is 3,409 lines containing six sales sections that duplicate /sales-analytics and five finance sections that duplicate /financial-reports, including a second complete commitments CRUD editor (:3017-3409) that has already diverged from the canonical one. Delete the commitments section outright and link to /financial-reports. Move or delete the sales sections. Drop the dead Xero P&L and bank-summary fetches from billing/financial-health. What survives is roughly 800 lines of genuine operational reporting (response time, retainer health, utilisation, request throughput) which is worth keeping and worth converting to DataTable, but only after the page stops being three pages. Also fix the mixed feature gating: filter REPORTS_SECTIONS by the resolved feature map so a denied section is absent rather than an error card, and add org scoping to the report endpoints before the first hire.

BLOCK 4 - hygiene, ~3d, any time. Collapse the two access editors (retire the /team slide-over, deep-link to the permissions pane) and relabel the /team Role column so it stops implying permission. Surface scheduledCalls on the /calls index so a client-booked kickoff is visible. Fix lib/ai-cost.ts:23-24 (Opus at $5/$25, not $15/$75) - a one-line fix that has been carried in memory for months and is currently overstating AI spend threefold. Strip the 18 em-dash page titles. Give /docs and /time a PageHeader. Delete the dead billing/monthly-email route.
